title: Finite open tests for uniform orders and homogeneous division
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero [def-weil-field] and $N$ be a smooth affine finite-type $k$-scheme with etale coordinates $w$ and $a\in N$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Fix regular functions $c_{i\gamma}$ on this single $N$, for $1\le i\le s$ and $\gamma\in\mathbf N^n$, and at $b\in N$ put $L_b=\kappa(b)$ and
$$f_{i,b}(W,Z)=\sum_\gamma T_b(c_{i\gamma})(W)Z^\gamma\in L_b[[W,Z]],$$
where $T_b$ is the centered Taylor map on $N$ [def-weil-residue-field] [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Fix a monotone diagram $D$ with ordered minimal vertices $(0,\alpha_i)$ and degrees $d_i=|\alpha_i|$, and assume that at $a$ the first exponents of $f_{i,a}$ are these vertices with nonzero coefficients. First exponents use total-degree lexicographic order with $W$ before $Z$. For each prefix of degree blocks let $Z^\ell$ be its essential variables, $D_\ell$ its restricted diagram, and $\Delta_i^\ell$ its first-vertex supports [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division]. Define
$$S=\{b\in N:c_{i\gamma,b}\in\mathfrak m_b^{d_i-|\gamma|}\text{ for all }|\gamma|<d_i\}.$$
Here $c_{i\gamma,b}$ is the germ and $\mathfrak m_b$ the local maximal ideal; zero has infinite order. Assume $a\in S$.
There is one neighbourhood $V$ of $a$ in $N$, obtained by inverting finitely many regular functions nonzero at $a$, on which the following hold for every $b\in S\cap V$: $\operatorname{ord}f_{i,b}=d_i$; and for every degree prefix and every total degree $t$ the initial forms of the corresponding $f_{i,b}$ have unique homogeneous division, with first-vertex quotient supports and remainder outside the prefix diagram in all variables $(W,Z)$. The finite functions to invert may be chosen as one degree-$d_i$ Taylor-coefficient derivative per $i$ that is nonzero at $a$, together with the supported homogeneous-division determinants [def-weil-matrix] [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant] for each restricted $D_\ell$ in degrees at most its finite stabilization bound $b(D_\ell)$. In these restricted determinants all complementary variables are set to zero. Every matrix entry is $0$, $1$, or a regular derivative of some $c_{i\gamma}$ divided by a factorial [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. Unique restricted division extends to all complementary variables, and no inversions indexed by unbounded degree or by all coefficients are needed. Prefixes with no essential variables and an empty vertex list are included. The assertion is compatible with residue-field extension.

proof.text: The constant Taylor coefficient identifies the coefficient of W^0 Z^gamma with evaluation of c_i,gamma. Nonzero first coefficients give the order witnesses; coefficient_first_exponent_determinants gives all the determinant tests. Thus every element of coefficientDivisionTests is nonzero at a. Evaluation of their product is nonzero, so a belongs to its principal open.

proof.text: A restricted coefficient is c_i,gamma in its homogeneous degree, and zero otherwise. The monomial-shift coefficient formula shows that every matrix entry is zero, one, or such a coefficient. Membership in the finite tests follows from membership in the corresponding image or biUnion.

proof.text: At a point b on the principal open every test evaluates nonzero, by map_prod and prod_ne_zero_iff. Apply coefficient_restricted_finite_tests to obtain all restricted divisions and their scalar extensions. The coefficient order lower bound and the nonzero vertex coefficient give equality of orders.

proof.text: Apply coefficient_restricted_to_full using the W-zero coefficient identities. For each residue extension j, injectivity and the coefficient formula imply order(map j f)=order(f); apply the same comparison over the extension field, and use injectivity to preserve every test nonvanishing.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q18-9d0da64f8 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node and every cited statement in full; the details are in review.md. Source: ILO VIII 2.3.11-2.3.13 (PDF pp.99-100) points the route to Bierstone-Milman; BM is not in the local literature, so the item is correctly marked agent-origin. The item's statement changes are justified. The old clause 'every matrix entry is a derivative/factorial' is false: remainder columns have entries 0 and 1. I checked the counterexample N=Spec Q, c_{1,1}=2, degree-0 matrix (1). The only citer, regular-hilbert-coefficient-data, uses only conclusions (1) and (2). Saying 'k a field' only makes explicit what was implicit. No target is weakened. Steps: (1) the Taylor and derivation nodes give the factorial coefficient formula, valid since the characteristic is 0. (2) The order bound holds because the Taylor map sends m_b^k into (W)^k, with witness u_i=c_{i alpha_i}. (3) The bijection (i,beta)->alpha_i+beta makes the matrix square. Lex order restricted to V-monomials is multiplicative, so the matrix at a is lower triangular with diagonal u_i(a) or 1. (4) The set of tests is finite; a nonzero determinant gives a basis in each tested degree, and stabilization (which covers prefixes and the restriction to essential variables) gives all degrees. (5) Because the vertices are zero in U, the diagram is N^U x D_l with supports N^U x Delta_i^l, and the new lemma (i)=>(ii) applies. (6) Edge cases and field extension are fine. New node: (i)=>(ii) by block-triangularity in U-degree; (ii)=>(i) by setting U=0 plus the count bijection. I tested zero H_i, s=0, m=0, r=0, a degree-0 vertex, and H=V+U. It is pure algebra, not a restatement of the item and not a duplicate: I compared it against homogeneous-continuous-formal-division, supported-formal-division, initial-diagram-stabilization, generic-monotone-diagram, stratum-minors, exact-block-projection and blowup-division-generators. Fixes: (B4) the new node's statement had \notin written with one JSON backslash three times, which reads as a newline plus 'otin'; I repaired all three. I also added inline citations [def-weil-field], [def-weil-matrix] and [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant] to the item statement to match its new stmt_deps.
